scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: The IT Department reports "switch0 (the IT-dept switch)
failed" -- they say the whole IT segment (192.168.1.0/24) is down because the
access switch connecting the IT hosts to their gateway stopped passing traffic, and
they want the switch replaced/restarted. Please confirm the switch failure.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The IT access switch (switch0) is operating normally. Evidence:
- Layer-3 reachability from IT hosts is intact. it_lab1 (192.168.1.3) can ping its default gateway router0 (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss (rtt ≈1.2 ms). it_hod (192.168.1.2) also reaches 192.168.1.1 cleanly, and intra-VLAN pings it_hod ↔ it_lab1 succeed.
- Inter-VLAN connectivity works through the gateway, proving end-to-end forwarding across the access switch: it_lab1 can ping office_pc (192.168.3.2) and internet host pc2 (128.168.0.2) with 0% loss.
- Router-facing tests confirm bidirectional reachability to IT hosts (router0 → it_lab4 0% loss).
- On switch0, the bridge is up and correctly plumbs both ports: br0 is UP with eth0 and eth1 enslaved (master br0). Physical links are healthy: ethtool on switch0 eth0 and eth1 reports “Link detected: yes,” full duplex, 10G speed. Router0’s IT interface (eth0 192.168.1.1/24) is UP and routing table is populated.

Mechanism: If the access switch were not passing traffic, IT hosts would fail to ARP/reach 192.168.1.1 and inter-VLAN pings would fail. None of these failure signatures are observed.

Localization: switch0 br0 bridging eth0 (to router0) and eth1 (to lan_it) is functional; router0 eth0 is operational.

Root cause: No current switch failure; likely a transient or host-specific issue, not reproducible now.

Corrective fix: No replacement/restart required. Recommend monitoring switch0 ports and counters, and checking cabling/NICs on any specific affected workstation if issues recur.
